sentences.text: The learned Counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner also does not intend to needlessly hold up the public work, but in this case, there is no acquisition of his land and the Petitioner cannot be forcefully and illegally removed from possession.

The learned Counsel for the Petitioner submits that the Petitioner will file an undertaking that the moment a notification is issued under Sub-Section (1) of Section 3-A of the Act of 1956, the Petitioner will also handover the possession without waiting for further formalities and will lodge such objection when such notification is issued.

11. According to us, since the Petitioner's land is not mentioned in both the notifications and the Award could not have been passed respect of the same, the petition deserves to be allowed and it could have been allowed today itself.

However, the learned Counsel for the Respondents has submitted that the petition be kept pending as the Respondents-Authorities will consider the position as to whether the Respondents- Authorities will issue a notification under Sub-Section (1)
of Section 3-A in respect of the subject land only and take further steps as per the Act of 1956.
To monitor these modalities, we issue Rule. Rule made returnable after twelve weeks.
The Respondents waive service.
13. The ad interim order granted earlier will continue with the following modifications:

(i) In view of our finding that the land bearing City Survey No. 359 has not vested with the Central Government under Section 3-D(2) of the Act of 1956, it is open to the Central Government to proceed to issue a notification under Section 3-A of the Act of 1956 in respect of the subject land and mention of the said land in the Award will not be considered as an impediment.
(ii) The Petitioner will then file an undertaking that the Petitioner will hand over vacant and peaceful possession to the Respondents.
(iii) Before taking possession and prior to possession being handed over, the joint measurement will be carried out.

2. Mr. Singh, the learned counsel appearing for National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) would draw our attention to the Notification dated 7 March 2024 issued under Sub Section 1 of Section 3-A of the Act of 1956.
Thus, immediately upon publication of Notification dated 7 March 2024 the Petitioner was supposed to file an undertaking for handing over vacant and peaceful possession of land in question to NHAI.
He has 5_wp_457_2023.docx however, failed to file such an undertaking despite issuance of Notification being brought to his knowledge.
So far as the joint measurement is concerned, our attention is invited to the statement of the Petitioner recorded during the course of joint measurement taken on 28 March 2024.

sentences.text: The measurement sheet indicates existence of one RCC building of three floors.
However, the measurement sheet does not indicate that the constructed structure is measured in any manner.
3. Accordingly, the concerned authority shall forthwith carryout the measurement of the construction, which is likely to be affected by the acquisition proceedings.
This would assist both the sides for determining the issue of compensation.
Let the exercise be carried out before the next date of hearing.
List the petition for further consideration on 11 June 2024.
Mr. Talekar, fairly submits that Petitioner shall not object to construction work being carried out in respect of vacant land to the extent it does not affect the constructed structure in any manner.
NHAI is accordingly permitted to carry out work on vacant land of Petitioner without touching the constructed structure.
The permission to take possession of constructed structure would be considered on the next date of hearing once the exercise of measurements of construction is completed.
